conviction_note: Q3 comps (+3.9%) are pre-released, so the print turns on three unseen things: EBITDA flow-through on a +5.6% check, the first fiscal-2026 outlook under the franchised model, and how the refinancing's interest saving is framed. The positives (comps above the FY range, an 11.5% loan replaced at about SOFR+325) roughly offset the negatives (a mechanical EBITDA guide reset, traffic slipping to -1.7%, peers saying Q4 started soft, beef inflation, a freed 18.6% activist block). The findings sum to -0.6 while the scaled number is +0.6. The gap comes from the reaction function: this name's last three full prints were bought (+21%, +18%, +33%), and about 9.5% of shares are short at 7 days to cover. Both pull p_up slightly above 50, so the two numbers disagree in sign and are both near zero.
bar: Q3 revenue consensus $254.0M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RRGB/earnings-forecasts) and $251.7M (Opencapital, https://www.opencapital.sh/stocks/rrgb/earnings/q3-2026): two sources roughly agree on about $252-254M. Q3 EPS consensus disagrees: -$0.43 (Benzinga), -$0.36 (Opencapital), and -$0.70 at Earnings Whispers (likely stale). Company guide (Aug 12, 2026, https://ir.redrobin.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/735/red-robin-gourmet-burgers-inc-reports-second-quarter-of): FY26 comps +0.5% to 1.5%, RLOP margin about 13.0%, Adj EBITDA $70-73M, capex $25-30M, all EXCLUDING the refranchising, with an update promised at closing. Q3 2025 comparables: revenue $265.1M, Adj EBITDA $7.6M, RLOP 9.9%. The implied Q3+Q4 FY26 EBITDA on the old guide is $23.8-26.8M (first 28 weeks were $46.2M). The EPS bar is disputed, so the reported-quarter findings are kept small; the revenue bar and the company guide are usable.
positioning_check: Short interest 1.79M shares, 7.1 days to cover, at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/rrgb; curvedtrading shows 1.8M and 7.1 days: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/rrgb/short-interest/). That is about 9.5% of the 18.9M shares outstanding, up from 1.6M (5.4 days) on 2026-09-15. No November settlement was found. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline, so there is no directional statement from the skew. Put/call open interest is 0.19 (call-heavy) on only 356 contracts total, with an ATM spread at 50% of mid, so the 16.3% implied move is indicative only. Run-up: -9.99% over 5 days and -6.67% over 20 days. The stock was $9.01 on 2026-11-11 per MarketBeat/Schwab and is $8.11 now, with no company news found in between. Holders: JCP 9.8% and Jumana 8.8% left the board on 2026-10-23 and terminated their group (13D/A 2026-10-27); Bandera Partners holds 6.1% (13G/A 2026-11-12, as of 2026-09-30).

findings.finding: Pre-released Q3 comparable restaurant revenue was +3.9% (check +5.6%, traffic -1.7%), the best since Q1 2023. That puts the 40-week comp at +1.5%, the top of the reaffirmed FY26 range of +0.5% to 1.5%. The unseen part is margin and EBITDA conversion: on Q3 2025's base ($7.6M Adj EBITDA, 9.9% RLOP margin), a roughly 4-point comp mostly carried by check should flow through at a high rate. That supports a Q3 EBITDA above the prior year and a raised FY comp guide, partly offset by marketing spend that rose to $10.4M from $6.4M in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the comp was pre-released on 2026-11-02 the stock moved -0.88% (baseline). The last three full prints, each a turnaround-evidence beat, were bought: +21.32% (2026-08-12), +18.18% (2026-05-19) and +33.06% (2026-02-25).
findings.why_not_priced: The comp is public and earned -0.88% on the day, so the top line is priced. What the market has not seen is the margin. With no EBITDA, RLOP or guidance in the Nov 2 release, the stock has drifted 10% lower in five sessions instead of re-rating on a comp at the top of the range. Had the market priced strong flow-through, the stock would be nearer its $10.59 52-week high than 23% below it.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://ir.redrobin.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/735/red-robin-gourmet-burgers-inc-reports-second-quarter-of): RLOP margin rose 20bp on a +1.3% comp, but EBITDA fell on marketing. The two point different ways on flow-through. NRN (https://www.nrn.com/casual-dining/red-robin-reports-best-same-store-sales-since-2023, 2026-11-03) repeats the same company document.

findings.finding: The refinancing that closed Oct 2 replaced a term loan of $167.2M at an 11.50% weighted rate (balance at 2025-12-28; margin SOFR+7.50% under the 2024 amendment) with a $115M JPMorgan facility: a $90M term loan and a $25M revolver at SOFR+275-350bp, initially +325bp, no floor. On the disclosed figures, annual cash interest falls from about $19M to about $7M. That is roughly $12M a year, or about $0.60 per share pre-tax against an $8.11 stock and about $153M market cap. The first quantified framing and any FY27 FCF commentary arrive on tonight's call. The Q3 GAAP line will also carry a loss on extinguishment, which is a one-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print in the baseline turned on interest expense. The Oct 5 refinancing announcement itself was not a print event in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The facility terms are public, but the saving has never been stated by the company and is not in any guidance. EPS consensus is still a loss of $0.36-0.43 for the quarter, and the two sources disagree, which says nobody has rebuilt the model on the new capital structure. If it were priced, the post-refi equity would trade on FCF and the stock would not have given back its 11 Nov level.
findings.independence: The prior-loan rate is from the borrowings disclosure (https://app.edgar.tools/companies/RRGB/disclosures/debt) and the 2024 amendment exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000117175924000033/rrgb-20240714xex106.htm), which are different documents from the new facility's release. The saving itself is my arithmetic.

findings.finding: The FY26 Adj EBITDA guide of $70-73M explicitly excludes the refranchising of 108 company restaurants, most of which closed by Sept 1 for $89.4M; 8 more are pending for $6.6M. Tonight's 'updated fiscal 2026 outlook reflecting its more franchised ownership model' will therefore mechanically lower the headline EBITDA range: restaurant-level profit leaves, royalties come in. The new number has no sourced consensus, and a headline cut risks being read as a miss before the interest saving is netted against it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance was reaffirmed on 2026-08-12, a print that moved +21.32%. No resolved print here carried a guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: No source carries a post-refranchising FY26 EBITDA expectation; the company never quantified the EBITDA it sold. If the market had a number, previews would cite one. Instead the targets (consensus $8.33, Hold, MarketBeat 2026-11-11) and the EPS estimates are scattered.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://ir.redrobin.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/735/red-robin-gourmet-burgers-inc-reports-second-quarter-of) states the exclusion and the promised update. It is the same company guidance, not an independent series.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Red Robin's Nov 2 release say casual dining's Q4 started weak. Dine Brands (Nov 4) said Applebee's 'began the fourth quarter soft', with traffic negative at both brands and guidance pinned to the low end. BJ's Restaurants (Nov 5) raised FY comps to about 4.7% only on its Q3 beat, implying a high-1% Q4 comp with a roughly 100bp calendar headwind, and fell about 5%. Red Robin's own traffic worsened from -0.4% in Q2 to -1.7% in Q3, with the whole comp carried by check (+5.6%). Q4 commentary on the call is exposed to the same softness.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no baseline record of RRGB reacting to quarter-to-date commentary specifically. BJRI traded -5.34% on Nov 5 on a raise that banked Q3 ahead of a thinner Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer statements made after Red Robin last spoke, and Red Robin's own Q4-to-date has not been given. The stock's 10% slide in five sessions may partly reflect this, which is why the finding is kept small.
findings.independence: This is a peer proxy, not a company number. BJ's (https://finviz.com/news/418010/bjs-restaurants-delivers-its-best-quarter-of-the-turnaround-but-the-guidance-raise-mostly-banks-q3-ahead-of-a-thinner-q4, 2026-11-05) is a separate source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: US ground beef is at or near record prices through 2026, about 58% above 2020 per government data cited Nov 5. Burger King, Chipotle, Shake Shack and Darden have all cited beef as a cost driver, and Shake Shack posted its first quarterly loss in three years. Dine Brands reported 5.4% commodity inflation at Applebee's in Q3. For a burger-centred menu this pressures the cost-of-sales line in the Q3 RLOP margin and in the FY26 margin guide of about 13.0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no resolved RRGB print that turned on commodity cost. In Q3 2025 RLOP expanded 90bp on labour efficiency (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000162828025051046/rrgb-20251005.htm).
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission that Red Robin has not quantified. The +5.6% check may already be the pass-through, so the finding is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The Dine Brands commodity figure (https://finviz.com/news/416264/dine-brands-misses-badly-pins-guidance-to-the-low-end-as-a-rejected-takeover-bid-takes-center-stage) is a peer data point pointing the same way.

findings.finding: JCP Investment Management (1.86M shares, 9.8%) and Jumana Capital (1.67M, 8.8%), together about 18.6% of the 18.9M shares, left the board on Oct 23. They waived any replacement designee and terminated their group agreement on Oct 27, saying their objectives were 'substantially achieved'. That frees a large block from board-related restrictions. No sale was reported in the 60 days to Oct 27, and no JCP 13D amendment has followed. The block is a ceiling on any post-print rally.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. This is the first print since the board exit.
findings.why_not_priced: The exit is public and was framed as mission-accomplished. The stock fell from $9.01 (Nov 11) to $8.11 with no news, but nothing links that slide to these holders, so it is not treated as evidence here.
findings.independence: The joint press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000095014226002871/eh260848407_ex9901.htm) is the same event. It is not independent.

findings.finding: Short interest of 1.79M shares at 7.1 days to cover (2026-09-30), about 9.5% of shares and rising from 1.6M two weeks earlier, sits against a call-heavy option book (put/call OI 0.19). On ~214k shares a day of turnover, a clean beat or guide has a squeeze mechanism, as the +21%, +18% and +33% reactions to the last three full prints show.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is visible to anyone, but a short base of about 7 days to cover cannot leave in one session, so it shapes the reaction regardless.
findings.independence: curvedtrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/rrgb/short-interest/) shows the same settlement. Same FINRA data.

findings.finding: The release was delayed from Nov 4 to Nov 18 and an NT 10-Q was filed on Nov 2, citing 'accounting and valuation work' for the refranchising and refinancing. The company says this is unrelated to any significant change in financial condition. EDGAR shows no item 4.02 or auditor change since August. The Q3 GAAP line will therefore carry gain/loss-on-sale and extinguishment items whose size is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None comparable. The Nov 2 announcement of the delay moved the stock -0.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: The delay is public and was explained. Only the size of below-the-line items is unknown, and they have no path to the guide.
findings.independence: The Nov 2 release (https://finviz.com/news/413576/red-robin-announces-preliminary-third-quarter-comparable-restaurant-revenue-reschedules-earnings-call-to-november-18-2026) gives the reason. It is the same company.

outside_window.finding: The remaining 8 Op Burgers restaurants, about $6.6M of proceeds, are expected to close by fiscal year end, pending liquor licence transfers.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew number. A call-heavy book (put/call 0.19), an implied move of 16.3%, a history of large up-moves on prints and a 10% five-day drawdown all lean toward an upside reaction. My findings net slightly negative because the guide reset and peer Q4 softness are unquantified risks, so I keep p_up near 50 rather than taking either side.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the JCP/Jumana overhang finding no longer leans on the no-news slide from $9.01; it was cut from -0.5 to -0.3.

Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks negatives): with about 9.5% of shares short at 7.1 days to cover, the peer Q4 finding went from -1.0 to -0.8, the beef proxy from -0.7 to -0.6 and the NT 10-Q one-off from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 5 (positioning does not file as evidence): the short-interest squeeze finding was trimmed from +0.5 to +0.3 and kept small.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, large reaction distribution): abs_move_pct raised from 14 to 15, with a 16.3% implied move and three of the last four full prints above 18%.
Lesson 6 (bar): the EPS bar is disputed, so the reported-quarter finding stays capped at 1.5; the revenue bar (two sources agree) and the company guide are used instead.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): left standing. This name has bought prints, so p_up stays slightly above 50 despite a negative findings sum.
